rounds.text: Current Infraprojects Ltd is deeply under-appreciated by the market, trading at a modest P/E of 14.4x that closely tracks the sector benchmark while delivering vastly superior fundamental performance [E1, E6]. The business boasts an exceptional return on capital, with ROCE reaching up to 30.7% and a stellar 3-year median ROE of 35%, completely eclipsing the broader sector median ROCE of 13.6% [E10, E17, E52]. Growth metrics are equally explosive, highlighted by a 3-year compounded sales growth of 41% and a staggering 3-year compounded profit growth of 113% [E12, E14]. This elite operational momentum is paired with a pristine balance sheet, evidenced by a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.16x alongside ongoing debt reduction from Rs 20 Cr to Rs 13 Cr [E26, E27]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow model establishes an intrinsic value implying a massive margin of safety of 63.7%, while a reverse DCF indicates that the current market price accounts for a paltry 4.0% earnings growth against a base-case expectation of 18.0% [E33, E34, E35]. Finally, strong domestic institutional backing is evident as domestic institutions increased their stake to 10.67% from 9.69% [E31]. Conceded: [E22], [E23], [E24], [E25], [E41].

Despite reported headline profitability, Current Infraprojects Ltd suffers from an alarming complete disconnect between accounting earnings and actual cash generation [E22]. Operating cash flow collapsed to negative Rs 12 Cr and free cash flow dropped to negative Rs 13 Cr in Mar 2026, meaning cash conversion sits at an abysmal -0.86x against reported profit [E22, E24]. This cash drain is directly tied to a severe deterioration in operational efficiency, as working capital days have nearly doubled from 64.2 days to 112 days [E41], and operating margins are officially flagged as inconsistent over both the last two years and last three quarters [E20, E21]. Furthermore, smart money is actively fleeing the counter as foreign institutions slashed their holdings by 3.34 percentage points down to 3.98%, driving a negative institutional money flow signal of -2.36 percentage points [E30, E32], while the company refuses to pay any dividend despite showing profits [E40]. conceded: [E14]

While the bear highlights a negative cash conversion of -0.86x and negative operating cash flow of Rs -12 Cr [E22, E23], these figures must be contextualized against a backdrop of explosive top-line and bottom-line scaling, including a 3-year compounded sales growth of 41% and a 3-year profit growth of 113% [E12, E14]. The bear points to a doubling of working capital days to 112 days and inconsistent margin flags [E20, E21, E41], yet the structural operating margin has expanded significantly from 5% three years ago to 12% in Mar 2026 [E19]. Regarding institutional outflows by foreign holders [E30], domestic institutions have stepped in by increasing their stake to 10.67% [E31], demonstrating local confidence in the business. Furthermore, the bear's concern over zero dividends [E40] is a common trait of high-growth companies actively reinvesting capital to drive superior returns, evidenced by an exceptional ROE of 27.5% to 35% and an ROCE above 22% [E9, E11, E17]. Finally, the balance sheet remains exceptionally robust with a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.16x after successfully reducing borrowings from Rs 20 Cr to Rs 13 Cr [E26, E27]. conceded: [E22]
